_readme: Followed writers. A Voice is a person, not a publication. This file is the source of truth for V1: adding or removing a Voice is a reviewed config change, not an in-app toggle, because the overnight GitHub Actions build is what reads it. See VOICES.md section 5 for the schema and README.md for how to add a Voice, resolve a provider id, and troubleshoot a source.

voices.name: Jonathan Haidt

sources.note: After Babel is multi-author (Haidt, Zach Rausch, Freya India and guests), so the feed URL alone proves nothing: each entry must carry his byline.

voices.note: Publishes across his own newsletter and third-party outlets. Cross-publication coverage is the job of a Perigon journalist id; resolve one with 'python -m src.voices.audit journalist "Jonathan Haidt"' and add it under provider_ids and a perigon_journalist source when PERIGON_API_KEY is configured.

sources.note: Jordan Peterson's first-party Blog category feed. The WordPress feed exposes the generic author 'admin', so the site's person-scoped Blog category, not that byline, establishes authorship. Coauthored Jordan Peterson posts remain qualifying work. Live-audited from GitHub Actions on 2026-09-06; the formerly configured Substack feed returned 403 from the runner.

voices.name: Conrad Black

sources.note: The New York Sun author archive is a valid first-party authorship surface, but on 2026-09-06 GitHub-hosted runners received HTTP 429 from the author page, its author feed, and the publication's tested general RSS endpoints. Disabled rather than evading publisher controls.

voices.note: Temporarily not an active Voice. Restore only through a supported source that works from the production runner (for example a stable provider journalist identity after the required provider key is configured). Hermes does not bypass paywalls or bot/rate-limit controls.

voices.name: George Monbiot
voices.note: The canonical-contributor case. The provider id attributes his work wherever it appears, including the ordinary morning Guardian fetch, at no extra request cost; the contributor query then guarantees a new column is seen even when it falls outside the sections Hermes already pulls.

voices.name: David Brooks
voices.note: The zero-request morning case. The NYT Top Stories opinion stream is already fetched for the Opinion desk, so his byline is matched inside a response Hermes pays for anyway. The alias is trusted only on nytimes.com; the same name on any other host is not this Voice. Release-time alerts are deliberately disabled because the watcher does not run the full NYT morning pool; set notify true only after adding an active watcher source for this Voice.
